searchText: The new testnet is live, we're past the merge epoch and just waiting for TTD now. All the info can be found here: https://kintsugi.themerge.dev on the new testnet, when i try to send 32 eth to deposit contract (0x4242424242424242424242424242424242424242) using metamask, i get an error: "invalid sender" ``` WARN [12-16|15:54:03.668] Served eth_sendRawTransaction conn=127.0.0.1:36608 reqid=1410551748998 t="217.144µs" err="invalid sender" ``` You need to change the network id on metamask right to 1337702 I have a geth/teku pair synced now hmm but just saw: ``` TTDD reached ERROR[12-16|17:53:24.324] ########## BAD BLOCK ######### Chain config: {ChainID: 1337702 Homestead: 0 DAO: <nil> DAOSupport: false EIP150: 0 EIP155: 0 EIP158: 0 Byzantium: 0 Constantinople: 0 Petersburg: 0 Istanbul: 0, Muir Glacier: <nil>, Berlin: 0, London: 0, Arrow Glacier: <nil>, MergeFork: 100, Engine: unknown} Number: 7234 Hash: 0x2db4178ecde1d213c68ffd24f220af055282844143c371a0efe60c938486abd4 0: cumulative: 21004 gas: 21004 contract: 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 status: 1 tx: 0xa1479c38a5eeb8197b9af5f17810c1074d89ff2ed27110cde13298ee0165c607 logs: [] bloom:  state: Error: invalid merkle root (remote: 99420179093b585df3b842b08fd90383ab8eb47f433465ccd92c516d6bffa280 local: a000b42cdd58db6ba2e124e293c4008e8de0af07e2d0a2f1b8b2c3674a37f8e0) ############################## ``` yeah, seems like besu is creating some invalid blocks at the moment seems we have problems -32000: invalid merkle root teku-geth seems good afaict which node are you looking? The block explorer https://beaconchain.kintsugi.themerge.dev/blocks?q=teku-geth right, looking good 🙂 are multi-block reorgs expected when a validator produces a bad block? I'm not seeing anything in my geth logs but my indexing code is detecting a reorg, havent fully debugged on my side yet though There are multi block reorgs on the beaconchain yes It looks like some nodes are not reacting to bad blocks very gracefully. Once there's a bad block, there are usually a few missed slots afterwards I'm getting bad blocks as well: Number: 7802 and 7816. Is it ok? (Geth+Lighthouse) Yes, Besu is creating bad blocks It's not an issue The only issue is that it seems that lighthouse won't reorg the chain if they receive a bad block, so they will only create a block on top once another client reorged the beacon chain ok, thanks! I don't see any related logs in geth but I have a toy program grabbing all the "details" of every block (e.g. receipts for all the txs, etc) that seemed to get back a non-JSON empty response for one of the tx receipts in block 7913, but I can't reproduce. Just curious if others are exercising the RPCs as well. I'm just constructing and sending transactions, no other RPC's for me Is there a preferred start/stop order between the EL and CL when restarting nodes? My guess is start EL then CL, stop is CL then EL, and that seems to be what works w/ my testing so far. Yes, that seems to be the best order. CL's are not really great a handling a missing EL
